title: Snell's Law and Critical Angle for Total Internal Reflection

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 12 — Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

expression: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂  ;  sinθc = n₂/n₁  (n₁ > n₂, denser to rarer)
explanation: Snell's law relates the angles of incidence and refraction to the refractive indices of the two media, governing how much a light ray bends crossing an interface. The critical angle θc is the specific angle of incidence (only possible going from a denser to a rarer medium) at which the refracted ray grazes along the interface (refraction angle = 90°); beyond this angle of incidence, no refraction occurs at all and light undergoes total internal reflection instead.

variables.meaning: Refractive indices of the first and second medium
Angle of incidence and angle of refraction

workedExample.scenario: Light travels from glass (n = 1.5) to air (n = 1) — find the critical angle.

commonMistakes: Trying to calculate a critical angle for light going from a rarer to a denser medium — total internal reflection (and hence a critical angle) is only possible when travelling from denser to rarer, never in the reverse direction.
Forgetting Snell's law uses the angle measured from the NORMAL to the surface, not from the surface itself — a very common geometric mix-up.
genZNote: Past the critical angle, light just gives up trying to leave and bounces back instead.
